author: Caden Perry
title: NWS issues severe thunderstorm warnings across Wisconsin June 24 - NewsBreak
text:
By Caden Perry ,
9 hours ago
The National Weather Service in La Crosse issued a severe thunderstorm warning at 2:20 p.m. on Wednesday, June 24 for Taylor, Clark, La Crosse and Vernon counties.
At 2:24 p.m., the Weather Service located a storm moving over La Crescent moving east.
The Weather Service station in Milwaukee/Sullivan issued severe thunderstorm warning for Dane County shortly after.
Finally, the Green Bay station issued a warning for Marathon County and Wood County for a separate weather pattern.
Meteorologists warn of winds as strong as 60 mph and hail as large as 1 inch in all each thunderstorm warning.
Hail damage to vehicles is expected as well as wind damage to roofs, siding and trees.
See weather radar for Wisconsin
What to do during a severe thunderstorm? The National Weather Service suggests that people stay inside in a sturdy building that can handle large hail, lightning, damaging wind, floods and possibly tornados.
The weather service also recommends staying away from windows and avoiding electric equipment and plumbing. Pets must be brought inside, and loose objects outside should be secured if there is time.
Avoid open spaces and get inside if possible. Cars can offer protection, but ensure tornadoes are not in the forecast.
This weather report was generated automatically using information from the National Weather Service and a story written and reviewed by an editor.
